Reference

Security and policy requirements

Every normative statement of the security pages with its id. The columns are: id, the statement (shortened), the page that explains it, and how to test it. A statement uses MUST, SHOULD or MAY as in RFC 2119 on its page; this table repeats only the subject. Rows whose test column names a fixture refer to the suite in Security testing.

You will need

  • The pages listed in the third column.

Decision labels

Label Subject Rows
D5 Sandbox on Linux only; other platforms run T1 only SEC-055, SEC-057
D12 process.run:sh is T1 only SEC-031
D23 Consent for hosts from settings SEC-074, SEC-312
D25 Origin consent for open-external SEC-043
G4, G5, G6, G8 Review dialog, bundled consent, revocation, key trust SEC-100 to SEC-124
D16, D17, D20, D21, D22, D24, SE10, C38 Cross-session, extension and replacement rules SEC-286 to SEC-306

Requirements

id statement page testable how
SEC-001 The host MUST treat every asset in this table as protected: reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-002 The host MUST validate all data that crosses boundaries B1 to B8 before using it. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-003 The kernel and T1 plugins share one address space. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-004 The decision: reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-005 The admin policy MAY forbid the combination for chosen plugins with [grants] deny_combinations, see Admin policy. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-006 Data-read and egress grant lists are fixed by the contract. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-007 Data passed between plugins through messages.peer, services, topics and extension points is outside grant enforcement. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-008 Same-user malware is out of scope. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-009 A root attacker, physical access, and a compromised kernel are out of scope. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-010 Malicious T1 code is out of scope. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-011 Third-party sandboxing on Windows and macOS is refused, not weakened. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-012 Side channels between a plugin and the machine hardware, such as cache timing between processes, are reduced but not eliminated. reference-threat-model Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-013 Every host call MUST be checked against the grants in force at that moment, for every tier except T0. security Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-014 A third-party package MUST never run in the Ilium process. security Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-020 The host MUST start one helper process per T2 or T3 plugin and per side. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-021 The helper runs in new user, mount, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces. reference-sandbox Hostile fixture reads /proc/self/ns/* and compares to the server's. All six differ.
SEC-022 The network namespace has no interface except a downed loopback. reference-sandbox Fixture calls socket+connect to loopback and to a public address. Both fail.
SEC-023 The mount namespace holds only: reference-sandbox Fixture lists /; only these paths exist. Executing a binary from /data fails with EACCES.
SEC-024 The helper sets no_new_privs, installs a seccomp allowlist, and drops every capability before it reads the first plugin byte. reference-sandbox Fixture calls prctl(PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS). Result is 1.
SEC-025 The sandbox is defence in depth. reference-sandbox Escape probe suite, see Security testing.
SEC-026 The helper's /proc shows only its own PID namespace. reference-sandbox Fixture reads /proc/1/environ (its own init) and the server's PID path. The second does not exist.
SEC-027 The helper's environment is rebuilt from an allowlist: reference-sandbox Fixture prints environ. Only the allowlist appears.
SEC-028 All file descriptors except the dispatcher channel and stdio on /dev/null are closed before the Wasmtime engine starts (close-range with no exceptions). reference-sandbox Fixture enumerates /proc/self/fd; only fds 0 to 2 and the channel remain. ioctl(0, TIOCSTI) fails.
SEC-029 A cgroup v2 leaf is created per helper with: reference-sandbox Fixture allocates past the limit; helper is killed; the log has the code.
SEC-030 Every row in this table MUST have the mitigation implemented. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-031 process.run and process.spawn need a grant for the exact program. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-032 Children of T2 and T3 plugins run in the same confinement as the helper and have no network. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-033 Environment keys are validated. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-034 A program may not resolve into package, data, cache, picked or any writable scope. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-035 Argument hazards. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-040 create-pane with a command from a T2 or T3 plugin needs the H grant panes.create-command:<program>. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-041 panes.lifecycle restart with a new command uses the same grant and the same confirmation. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-042 agent.signatures rules: reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-043 open-external file targets: reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-044 clipboard.write: reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-045 notify.desktop: reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-046 Regular expressions supplied by plugins (output filters, settings pattern, schema pattern, when expressions) MUST be compiled with a linear-time engine that has Rust regex semantics: reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-050 The server MUST treat every message from a helper as hostile. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-051 The server MUST enforce a maximum message size of 4 MiB (8 MiB for terminal-view frames) and a rate of 5,000 messages per second per helper. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-052 A malformed message (bad framing, bad UTF-8, a schema violation, an unknown message kind, an out-of-range resource handle) kills the helper and counts as a failure toward the restart-and-disable rule. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-053 Wasmtime configuration, for T1 and for the helper: reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-054 Compiled module cache. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-055 If the host cannot create the sandbox exactly as specified, T2 and T3 plugins MUST refuse to load with error code sandbox.unavailable. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-056 Running as root. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
SEC-057 Platform matrix. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite

SEC-059 Hard links. reference-sandbox Integration test with the hostile-plugin fixture suite
